# Deep Dive: Trade Deficits and Capital Flows

Report 160 | Published 2025-04-13 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2025-4-13/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/160.json)

Trade imbalances, tariff stress and selected investments.

The defensive February positioning and subsequent negotiation expectation receive support. The reserve-dollar explanation overstates the necessity of trade deficits, and NIIP valuation effects materially complicate its ownership narrative. The April outflow diagnosis has some evidence but omits FX hedging. Explicit multi-year rotation, ITUB and gold horizons remain unfinished; the AMD option outcome is conditional on execution.

**Coverage:** All sections read, including extensive quotations of earlier reports, historical crisis comparisons, tariff scenarios, the executed-position disclosures and long-horizon gold/ITUB views. Repeated material claims are retained but linked by family. No actual brokerage returns inferred from the put example.

### 160-C02

**Deficits supply dollars.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | reserve-currency-trade-deficit |
| Source blocks | 13, 19, 31, 33, 93 |
| Thesis family | reserve-currency-trade-deficit |

A reserve issuer need not run a trade deficit to supply dollar credit. Gross bank financing, including offshore creation, is distinct from net saving and trade flows. Reserve demand can influence exchange rates, but the stated necessity is false.

**Direction:** Contradicted for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [How does international capital flow?](https://www.bis.org/publications/working-paper-890-how-does-international-capital-flow) | Kumhof, Rungcharoenkitkul and Sokol / BIS | 2020-10-01 | Verified in the audit

Working paper distinguishes gross financing from net saving: US and non-US banks create dollar credit without a necessary US current-account deficit. Authors views, not an institutional policy position.

### 160-C04

| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | dollar-debt-service |

For fixed unhedged dollar debt and unchanged local revenue, dollar appreciation increases local-currency servicing cost. Borrowers with dollar revenues or hedges are exceptions.

**Direction:** Supported for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Deductive assessment:**

- Dollar obligation D fixed
- No hedge or matching dollar revenue
- Local revenue fixed

Local servicing cost is e D; an increase in local-currency-per-dollar e raises the burden.
